facts.statement: Lianghusuchus is an extinct genus containing only one species of crocodilian.
facts.quote: Lianghusuchus is an extinct monospecific genus of crocodilian.

facts.statement: The species Lianghusuchus hengyangensis was named in 1948.
Fossils of Lianghusuchus date to the Eocene and were found in Hunan, China.
facts.quote: Fossils date back to the Eocene and have been found from Hunan, China.

facts.statement: Originally classified in the crocodile family Crocodylidae, Lianghusuchus was later reclassified into the alligator family Alligatoridae based on a 1999 study.
facts.quote: It was originally considered a crocodile belonging to the family Crocodylidae, but was later considered a member of the alligator family Alligatoridae in a 1999 phylogenetic study by Christopher Brochu.

facts.statement: Lianghusuchus belongs to the parent group Alligatoridae.
Lianghusuchus lived between 56 and 37.71 million years ago during the Ypresian to Bartonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Bartonian (56 to 37.71 million years ago)
